Children explain how each fruit is attained, and the second raises and answers objections and reconciles a conflicting scriptural statement.
Each child is a one-line pointer to the relevant verse lines with no discussion.
Children explain substantial and aggregate particles with reasoning, a citation and a refuted objection.
Each child cites its verse and proves the category by syllogism, and the last adds an extended analysis of mental-factor counts per mind.
Definition and division are short, but the third child is a long nine-part analysis with Vaibhasika-Sautrantika debate and proofs.
Definition with citation and a one-line division, but the third child argues the ethical status, times and realms of non-possession with proofs and a raised doubt.
Definition with verse citation and division, then a child that resolves doubts through a Vaibhasika argument and the master's rebuttal.
Children define each absorption and analyse its seven distinguishing features, with justification of qualifiers and of the bodily support.
Children define the life faculty with citations, analyse its three kinds with a scriptural objection and reply, and explain its function.
The general-meaning child is a long six-part analysis of the six causes with definitions, debate and compatibility analysis.
After a short definition and list, children define each fruit with citations, map fruits to causes with a refuted view, and resolve doubts about their compatibility.
Two children are one-line definition and list, but others define each condition with reasoning on compatibility and explain when each acts and what each produces.
Two children enumerate the twelvefold and twentyfold divisions of mind, and the third argues with citations which division is wider.
Children explain at length the eight occasions and how the twelve and twenty minds serve as immediately preceding conditions, with reasons.
Children explain the form and formless realms, giving their abodes and how they arise, with syllogistic proofs and a gloss of a particle.
